response.title: Harborlight in FY2026 and the Case for a Sixth Site

segments.heading: The big picture
segments.text: Harborlight reached more adult learners in fiscal year 2026 than the year before. Now staff want the board to fund a sixth site. Here are the basics. Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners across five neighborhood sites. The year before, it enrolled 936. Of this year's learners, 412 were working toward a high school equivalency credential. And 389 were English language learners. The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21.

segments.heading: How learners did
segments.text: Learners made real progress. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels. The CASAS assessment measured that gain. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. No year in the organization's history topped that. One learner at the Riverside site summed it up. Quote. "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring." End quote.

segments.heading: People and money
segments.text: Next, the people and the money. A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. The average tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight has 11 full-time staff. Four of them are site coordinators. Operating expenses for fiscal year 2026 came to $1,420,000. Program costs made up 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants brought in $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. The cost per learner was $1,237.

segments.heading: Two worries
segments.text: Two problems need attention. The first is the waitlist. At year end, 287 adults were waiting for a spot. Most of them were at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. On average, they waited nine weeks. The second is reserves. The treasurer reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months. So reserves fall short of the target as the board weighs the budget request.

segments.heading: What staff are asking
segments.text: Last comes the request. Staff recommend that the board approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. That budget adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. It also adds two site coordinators. Staff estimate the sixth site would serve 180 more learners a year. They also estimate it would cut the waitlist in half. The board asked staff for a one-page summary of the request for the October 21 board meeting. Board members also want a short deck to share with funders when they discuss the sixth site.

response.recap: Keep three things in mind. One: Harborlight enrolled 1,148 learners, and Seventy-one earned a high school equivalency credential, the most in its history. Two: 287 adults are waiting for a spot, and reserves stand at 3.2 months against a target of 4 months. Three: staff want an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 to open a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library.
